name: Cranio-cervical dystonia with laryngeal and upper-limb involvement
aliases: Segmental dystonia involving cranio-cervical region and upper limbs
Cervical dystonia with laryngeal and upper limb symptoms

criteria.description: Presence of sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal movements or postures in cranio-cervical region
Evidence of laryngeal dystonia manifesting as voice breaks, strained or strangled voice quality
Involvement of upper limb muscles with dystonic posturing or tremor
No clinical or imaging evidence of neurodegenerative disease
Exclusion of secondary causes such as drug-induced or structural lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of sustained involuntary muscle contractions in cranio-cervical region with both laryngeal and upper limb dystonia manifestations, after exclusion of secondary causes and neurodegenerative diseases.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; electrophysiological studies may support but are not mandatory.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal; used to exclude structural lesions
Cervical spine imaging to rule out compressive causes
other: Electromyography (EMG) may show abnormal muscle activation patterns
Laryngoscopy may reveal spasmodic contractions of vocal cords

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated laryngeal involvement without cervical or limb dystonia
Voice symptoms predominate without abnormal head posturing
Presence of parkinsonism features such as bradykinesia and rigidity
History of drug exposure, trauma, or structural brain lesions
Imaging abnormalities or metabolic derangements present

redFlags: Rapid progression of symptoms over weeks
Presence of additional neurological signs such as weakness or sensory loss
Respiratory compromise due to laryngeal spasms
references: Albanese A, et al. Phenomenology and classification of dystonia: a consensus update. Mov Disord. 2013.
Jinnah HA, et al. Dystonia: clinical features and diagnosis. Neurol Clin. 2015.
Orphanet Report on ORPHA:420485 Cranio-cervical dystonia with laryngeal and upper-limb involvement.
